title: Protective equipment and safe carry conditions
subtitle: Eye and ear protection, and how to carry your handgun

lines: This episode covers protective equipment, and the safe carry conditions.
The condition in which you carry your firearm is of vital importance to your own safety and those around you.
PPE stands for Personal Protection Equipment.
On a shooting range, you must always use both eye and ear protection.

scenes.heading: Eye protection
bullets: A ricochet, muzzle-blast or ejected case
Can permanently damage your eyesight
Nicks and scratches on shooting glasses
Proof that eye protection is necessary
lines: A ricochet, muzzle-blast, or a case being ejected from a handgun can strike you in the eye.
That can cause permanent damage to your eyesight.
Look at the shooting glasses of an experienced shooter, and you will notice many nicks and scratches.
These nicks and scratches are proof that eye protection is necessary on the shooting range.

scenes.heading: Ear protection
bullets: A gunshot can permanently damage hearing
Occasional shooter, outdoor range: earplugs
Regular shooters: earmuffs recommended
Indoor range: earmuffs must be used
Never practise without ear protection

lines.text: The sound made by a firearm discharging is enough to cause permanent damage to your hearing.
Earplugs of plastic, foam or sponge are good enough for the occasional shooter using an outdoor range.
For regular shooters, it is recommended that earmuffs are used.
Earplugs are not sufficient hearing protection on indoor shooting ranges.

lines: On an indoor range, earmuffs must be used to protect not only the eardrum, but also the bone behind the ear.

lines.text: Under no circumstances should you practise without any form of ear protection.

scenes.caption: PPE: earmuffs and shooting glasses
lines: Eye and ear protection is essential at all times when on the shooting range.
Some people believe that firing without ear protection will help them get used to the sound of the gunshot.
This is not true!
If you find yourself getting used to the sound of the gunshot, you are going deaf!

lines.text: Now, carry conditions for the semi-automatic pistol.
Conditions one to three each describe the magazine.
They say whether there is a round in the chamber.
They say whether the hammer is back or forward.
And whether the safety catch is on or off.

scenes.heading: Carry conditions: semi-automatic pistol
bullets: Loaded magazine, round in chamber, hammer back, safety catch on
Loaded magazine, round in chamber, hammer forward, safety catch off
Loaded magazine, empty chamber, hammer forward, safety catch off
No live ammunition in the firearm at all
lines: There are four basic carry conditions for a semi-automatic pistol.

lines.text: Condition one. A loaded magazine, a round in the chamber, the hammer is back and the safety catch is on.
Condition two. Loaded magazine, round in the chamber, hammer forward, safety catch off.
Condition three. Loaded magazine, empty chamber, hammer forward, safety catch off.
Condition four. No live ammunition in the firearm at all.

lines: Any live ammunition is carried separate from the firearm.
This is the recommended condition when transporting firearms in the boot of your car.

scenes.caption: Condition 1 and Condition 2
lines: Here are conditions one and two in the book's photos.
In condition one, at the top, the hammer is back and the safety catch is on.
In condition two, below it, the hammer is forward and the safety catch is off.

scenes.heading: Take note: Condition One
bullets: Carry it in a holster securely attached to your body
The most ready, and the most dangerous
Condition Two or Three is much safer

lines.text: When carrying a firearm in Condition One, it should be carried in a holster securely attached to your body.
Although this is the most ready condition of the firearm, it is also the most dangerous carry condition.

lines: One should think very carefully before deciding to carry in Condition One.

lines.text: Condition Two or Three is much safer.

scenes.heading: Transporting any firearm
bullets: Transport it in a manner that is safe
Transport it unloaded
Not under your direct control: approved gun safe
lines: When transporting any firearm, it should be transported in a manner that is safe.
The firearm should be transported in an unloaded condition.
At any time when the firearm is not under your direct control, it must be locked away in an approved gun safe.

lines.text: There is only one way that a revolver can be carried for self-defence.
It should be carried with a fully loaded cylinder.
The hammer should be forward.
And it should be in a holster securely attached to your person.

scenes.heading: Misconception: an empty chamber under the hammer
bullets: Myth: empty chamber under the hammer is safer
1. A transfer bar between hammer and frame
2. The cylinder turns when the trigger is squeezed
Two empty chambers: only three shots

lines.text: Some people believe it is safer to carry a revolver with an empty chamber under the hammer.

lines: This is not true, for two reasons.

lines.text: One. There is a transfer bar between the hammer and the frame of the revolver.

lines: It ensures that if the revolver is dropped, the hammer cannot make contact with the firing-pin.

lines.text: Two. When you squeeze the trigger on the revolver, the cylinder turns.

lines: So leaving the chamber under the hammer empty will not help prevent an accident if the trigger is squeezed.
It is the chamber next to the one under the hammer that will fire first.

lines.text: It would be unwise to leave the first two chambers empty.

lines: That reduces the available ammunition to only three shots, which may not be enough in a life threatening situation.

rule.label: Remember
rule.text: When you are carrying a firearm in public it is a legal requirement that it must be concealed.

lines: And remember!
When you are carrying a firearm in public, it is a legal requirement that it must be concealed.

scenes.question: What is carry condition three?
options: Loaded magazine, round in chamber, hammer back, safety catch on
Loaded magazine, empty chamber, hammer forward, safety catch off
No live ammunition in the firearm at all
lines: The exam asks about conditions one and three.
So, what is carry condition three?
reveal: Condition three: loaded magazine, empty chamber, hammer forward, safety catch off.
Condition one has a round in the chamber, the hammer back and the safety catch on.

scenes.question: Why not only earplugs on an indoor range?
options: They don't protect the bone behind the ear
They block the Range Officer's commands
lines: Why should you not only use earplugs on an indoor shooting range?
reveal: On an indoor range, earmuffs must be used to protect not only the eardrum, but also the bone behind the ear.

points: PPE: eye and ear protection on a range
Condition One: most ready, most dangerous
Revolver: fully loaded, hammer forward, in a holster
In public: it must be concealed
lines: So, always use both eye and ear protection on a shooting range.
On an indoor range, use earmuffs, not only earplugs.
Know the four carry conditions for the semi-automatic pistol.
Condition One is the most ready, and the most dangerous.
Carry a revolver with a fully loaded cylinder, the hammer forward, in a holster securely attached to your person.
And in public, it is a legal requirement that your firearm must be concealed.
